title: Objects, iterators & reusable components
outcome: Represent state and stream data through well-defined Python interfaces.

steps.title: 1. Choose objects where useful
steps.text: A class packages state and operations. Do not add a class merely to use syntax. A dataclass can express a record with equality and a clear constructor.

steps.title: 2. Keep instance state independent
steps.text: Mutable defaults must be created per instance. dataclasses.field(default_factory=list) creates a fresh list. Frozen records reject ordinary attribute assignment, but freezing is not deep immutability.

steps.title: 3. Iterators are consumable
steps.text: An iterable can provide an iterator. Iterators yield values until exhausted; generators express lazy iteration using yield. Do not promise a reusable list when returning a one-shot stream.

steps.title: 4. Small interfaces enable testing
steps.text: A collector can be any object implementing the method required by the contract. Use composition and explicit dependencies before elaborate inheritance.

steps.title: 5. Test lifetime and reuse
steps.text: Test two instances, repeated calls, exhaustion, empty streams and cleanup. Output checks alone do not establish a good design; explain why the interface fits.

tasks.title: Resource context manager
contract: Define Managed(resource). __enter__ returns the resource; __exit__ calls resource.close() exactly once and does not suppress exceptions.
hints: Identify what must change and what must stay unchanged in this task: resource context manager.
Return the resource from enter and ensure exit handles cleanup without unintentionally suppressing exceptions.
Compare the implementation with case 02-exception. Trace the supplied inputs and the exact return/output type before changing the code.

cases.setup:
class R:
    calls=0
    def close(self):self.calls+=1
r=R()
cases.check:
with Managed(r) as value:
    assert value is r
expect(r.calls,1)
